sentences.text: Why? Who's in charge? And what comes next?
Its president and parliament were elected in 2019, and they're still there.
Why? Martial law. Since Russia's full-scale invasion, it bans every vote.
How they got there sounds made up.
Every citizen from 18 can vote, even from abroad.
You tick one name. Over half wins, or the top two face a run-off.
In 2019, TV comedian Volodymyr Zelensky won the run-off with 73%.
Then it got stranger: his party, named after his TV show, won parliament outright.
The Rada makes the laws and picks who runs the government.
In July, it chose a new prime minister.
When martial law ends, you'll tick a party and can write in a candidate's number.
And the 26 grey seats? Occupied districts, where no vote could be held.
Should Ukraine vote before the war ends?
